questions.question: A shopkeeper offers two successive discounts of 18% and 15% on a frock whose marked price is ₹1,000. What is the final selling price (in ₹) of the frock?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective **Selling Price percentage** = (100 − 18)% × (100 − 15)%

Effective **Multiplier** = 0.82 × 0.85 = 0.697

**Final Selling Price** = 1000 × 0.697 = 697

**∴ The correct answer is ₹697.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = ₹1,000

**Discount 1 (d₁)** = 18%

**Discount 2 (d₂)** = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Final Selling Price = MP × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59df9225b622576241ddf7b7fc82f118d4ffb5e2d736aceed2bf67b736a808b8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Price** after 1st discount = 1000 − (18% of 1000)

⇒ **Price** after 1st discount = 1000 − 180 = ₹820

⇒ **Final Selling Price** = 820 − (15% of 820)

⇒ **Final Selling Price** = 820 − 123 = ₹697

**∴ The correct answer is ₹697.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

The single equivalent discount for two successive discounts x% and y% is given by (x + y − xy/100)%.

Marked Price and Cost Price Relation

The relationship is given by: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%).

Effective Percentage Change

For successive changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is (a + b + ab/100)%, where negative values represent decreases/discounts.

questions.question: The sum of all interior angles of a regular polygon is 1800°. How many diagonals does the polygon have?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Number of **sides (n)** in a regular polygon − 2 = (Sum of interior angles) ÷ 180° ⇒ n − 2 = 1800 ÷ 180 = 10 ⇒ n = 12 Number of **diagonals** = [n × (n − 3)] ÷ 2 ⇒ [12 × (12 − 3)] ÷ 2 = 6 × 9 = 54 **∴ The correct answer is 54 diagonals.**

questions.question: A Company produces 1,520 packets of noodles in 5 hours. How many packets will it produce in 17 hours at the same rate?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **5 hr**, the company produces **1520 packets**.

Find the **packets produced in 1 hr**: 1520 ÷ 5 = 304.

Find the production for **17 hr**: 304 × 17.

Calculation: 304 × 17 = 5168.

**∴ The correct answer is 5168 packets.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Production in 5 hr (P₁) = **1520 packets**

Time period 1 (T₁) = **5 hr**

Time period 2 (T₂) = **17 hr**

Since the rate of production is constant, this is a case of **Direct Proportion**.

**Formula Used:**

(Packets₁ / Time₁) = (Packets₂ / Time₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5df1570f17c71bbfc138f25f107531f676632932c83099bdd1339ec975f475e4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Rate = P₁ / T₁

⇒ Rate = 1520 ÷ 5

⇒ Rate = 304 packets/hr

⇒ P₂ = Rate × T₂

⇒ P₂ = 304 × 17

⇒ P₂ = 5168

**∴ The correct answer is 5168 packets.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

Two quantities are in direct proportion if an increase in one leads to a proportional increase in the other, expressed as x/y = k (constant).

Unitary Method

A technique where you find the value of a single unit first (e.g., 1 hour) and then multiply to find the value for the required number of units.

Rate of Work

Rate = Total Work ÷ Total Time. In this problem, the rate of production is the number of packets produced per unit time.

questions.question: The largest four-digit number which when divided by 15, 12 and 14 leaves remainder 5 in each case is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of divisors 15, 12, and 14, which is 420.

Divide the largest 4-digit number (9999) by 420 to find the **remainder**: 9999 ÷ 420 ⇒ Remainder = 339.

Largest 4-digit multiple of 420 = 9999 − 339 = 9660.

Required number = **Multiple + Common Remainder** = 9660 + 5 = 9665.

**∴ The correct answer is 9665.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors: 15, 12, 14

Common Remainder (R) = 5

Target: **Largest 4-digit number** (N ≤ 9999)

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = [LCM(Divisors) × k] + Remainder

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20cead9370201f9ec21761084aea913120a4c2cd51233f7fd5aef47ab5bffee0.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization: 15 = 3 × 5, 12 = 2² × 3, 14 = 2 × 7

⇒ **LCM** = 2² × 3 × 5 × 7 = 4 × 3 × 35 = 420

⇒ Divide 9999 by 420 to find the nearest multiple:

⇒ 9999 = 420 × 23 + 339

⇒ Largest multiple = 420 × 23 = 9660

⇒ Required number = 9660 + 5

⇒ Required number = 9665

**∴ The correct answer is 9665.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Common Remainder

When a number N is divided by a, b, and c and leaves the **same remainder R** in each case, the general form is N = LCM(a, b, c) × k + R.

LCM and Different Remainders

If the remainders are r₁, r₂, r₃ such that (a−r₁) = (b−r₂) = (c−r₃) = d (constant difference), then N = LCM(a, b, c) × k − d.

HCF and Remainder

To find the **largest number** that divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder R, find the HCF of (x−R), (y−R), and (z−R).

questions.question: A, B, and C start a business by investing ₹60,000, ₹80,000, and ₹1,20,000, respectively. After one year, the total profit earned is ₹78,000. By how much does C’s share exceed B’s share?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit ratio of A, B, and C = 60,000 : 80,000 : 1,20,000 = 3 : 4 : 6

Total units = 3 + 4 + 6 = 13 units

Given: 13 units = ₹78,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹6,000

Required difference (C − B) = (6 − 4) = 2 units

Value = 2 × 6,000 = ₹12,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Capital of A = **₹60,000**

Capital of B = **₹80,000**

Capital of C = **₹1,20,000**

**Total Profit** = **₹78,000**

**Formula Used:**

In a partnership business, **Profit Ratio** = Capital × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d81f08a07c4c6565204e570aa1cd225e94fafe62016ca87a8ccc837952c0afa.png] 

**Calculations:**

Since the time period for all partners is 1 year, the profit will be divided in the ratio of their investments.

⇒ Profit Ratio (A : B : C) = 60,000 : 80,000 : 1,20,000

⇒ Ratio = 6 : 8 : 12 = 3 : 4 : 6

⇒ Total sum of ratios = 3 + 4 + 6 = 13 units

⇒ 13 units = ₹78,000

⇒ 1 unit = 78,000 ÷ 13 = ₹6,000

⇒ B’s share = 4 × 6,000 = ₹24,000

⇒ C’s share = 6 × 6,000 = ₹36,000

⇒ Difference = C’s share − B’s share = 36,000 − 24,000 = ₹12,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Profit Division

If partners invest C₁, C₂, C₃ capitals for times T₁, T₂, T₃, the profit is shared in the ratio (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂) : (C₃ × T₃).

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A **Working Partner** receives a fixed salary or percentage for managing the business, while the remaining profit is shared according to investment ratios.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest capital for different time durations, it is termed a compound partnership, and time must be multiplied with capital for calculations.

questions.question: Two buses start at the same time from two towns that are 264 km apart and travel towards each other along the same highway. The first bus travels at a speed of 22 km/h, while the second bus travels at a speed of 26 km/h. After how much time will they meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative speed** (opposite direction) = 22 + 26 = 48 km/h.

**Meeting time** = Total **distance** ÷ Relative **speed**.

Meeting time = 264 ÷ 48 = 5.5 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.5 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **distance** between two **towns** = 264 km

**Speed** of the first **bus** (S₁) = 22 km/h

**Speed** of the second **bus** (S₂) = 26 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = **Distance** ÷ Relative **Speed**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab4cc2ab4118f5c82490c70955056baeccbfb5169b9fa8b065c181125e8de95a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since the **buses** are traveling towards each other, they are in **opposite directions**.

⇒ Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂

⇒ Relative Speed = 22 + 26 = 48 km/h

⇒ **Time taken** to meet = 264 ÷ 48

⇒ **Time taken** = 132 ÷ 24 = 66 ÷ 12 = 11 ÷ 2

⇒ **Time taken** = 5.5 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 5.5 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Rules

For two objects with speeds **u** and **v**: if moving in the **opposite direction**, Relative Speed = u + v; if moving in the **same direction**, Relative Speed = |u − v|.

Average Speed Formula

When a person travels equal distances at speeds **x** and **y**, the **average speed** for the whole journey is (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Time and Distance Relation

**Distance** = Speed × Time. For a constant **distance**, **speed** is inversely proportional to **time** (S ∝ 1/T).

questions.question: A tank can be filled by pipe P in 8 hours and by pipe Q in 4 hours. If they open alternately for one hour each with Q starting first, what is the total time taken to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency of **Pipe P** = 1 unit/hr and **Pipe Q** = 2 units/hr (Total 8 units).

Work done in 1 cycle (2 hours: Q then P) = 2 + 1 = 3 units.

Work done in 2 cycles (4 hours) = 3 × 2 = 6 units.

Remaining work = 8 − 6 = 2 units, which **Pipe Q** fills in exactly 1 hour.

Total time = 4 + 1 = 5 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time for **Pipe P** = 8 hr, **Pipe Q** = 4 hr.

**Method:** LCM method to find **Total Work** and **Efficiency**.

⇒ **Total capacity** of the tank = LCM(8, 4) = 8 units.

⇒ In the 1st hour, **Pipe Q** is opened: Work done = 2 units.

⇒ In the 2ⁿd hour, **Pipe P** is opened: Work done = 1 unit.

⇒ Total work done in **2 hours** = 2 + 1 = 3 units.

⇒ Total work done in **4 hours** (2 such cycles) = 3 × 2 = 6 units.

⇒ **Remaining work** = 8 − 6 = 2 units.

⇒ In the 5th hour, it is **Pipe Q**'s turn again.

⇒ Time taken by **Pipe Q** to fill 2 units = 2 ÷ 2 = 1 hr.

⇒ **Total time taken** = 4 hr + 1 hr = 5 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its efficiency is 1/x of the tank per hour. For emptying pipes, efficiency is taken as negative.

Alternate Work Concept

When pipes work alternately, calculate the combined work in one full cycle (sum of individual hours) and then determine how many full cycles fit into the total work.

Total Time Calculation

Total Time = (Number of full cycles × hours per cycle) + (Remaining work ÷ Efficiency of the next pipe in sequence).

questions.question: A bookseller bought 7 identical sets of books at ₹375 each. He sold 3 sets at a profit of 16% per set and the remaining sets at a profit of 24% per set. What was his total profit (in ₹) from selling all the sets?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total profit is calculated using the **weighted average** of the profit percentages.

Overall Profit % = [ (3 × 16) + (4 × 24) ] ÷ 7 = (48 + 96) ÷ 7 = 144/7 %

Total Profit = (Total CP) × (Overall Profit %)

Total Profit = (7 × 375) × (144 ÷ 7 ÷ 100) = 375 × 1.44 = ₹540

**∴ The correct answer is ₹540.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of **1 set** = ₹375

Number of sets sold at **16% profit** = 3

Remaining sets sold at **24% profit** = 7 − 3 = 4

**Formula Used:**

Profit = CP × Profit%

Total Profit = (Profit per set₁ × n₁) + (Profit per set₂ × n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f48c729785c47144c62b368513654dae0a1c8318a331e001eeed3086663bb3e3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit from **3 sets** = 3 × (16 ÷ 100 × 375) = 3 × 60 = ₹180

⇒ Profit from **4 sets** = 4 × (24 ÷ 100 × 375) = 4 × 90 = ₹360

⇒ **Total Profit** = ₹180 + ₹360 = ₹540

**∴ The correct answer is ₹540.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Profit Percentage

It is the total profit earned on all items divided by the total cost price of all items, multiplied by 100: (Total Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100.

Weighted Average Profit

When quantities are different, the overall profit % = (n₁p₁ + n₂p₂ + ...) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ...), where n is the quantity and p is the profit %.

Relation between CP and SP

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit. If profit is given in percentage, SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: If the salary of a person is first increased by 15% and thereafter decreased by 12%, what is the net change in his salary?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change formula = a + b + (a × b)/100.

Here, a = +15 (increase) and b = −12 (decrease).

Net change = 15 − 12 + (15 × −12)/100 = 3 − 1.8 = 1.2%.

Since the result is positive, it is a 1.2% **increase**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.2% increase.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **increase** in salary = 15%

Subsequent **decrease** in salary = 12%

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be9d15b19eb5739018d61eb4260f119306f03fc47a629b422a53eef32aa8b76a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial **salary** of the person be ₹100.

⇒ Salary after 15% **increase** = 100 + (15% of 100) = 100 + 15 = ₹115.

⇒ Salary after 12% **decrease** = 115 − (12% of 115)

⇒ New Salary = 115 − (12/100 × 115) = 115 − 13.8 = ₹101.2.

⇒ **Net Change** in salary = 101.2 − 100 = 1.2.

⇒ Net percentage change = (1.2 / 100) × 100 = 1.2%.

⇒ Since the final value is more than the initial value, it is an **increase**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.2% increase.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net change is given by [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

Multiplying Factor Method

For an increase of r%, the factor is (1 + r/100). For a decrease, it is (1 − r/100). Net change = (Factor₁ × Factor₂ − 1) × 100.

Applications in Revenue

This logic is widely used in questions involving Price × Consumption = Expenditure or Length × Breadth = Area.

questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus are mutually perpendicular and bisect each other. One diagonal is 10 cm longer than the other. If the area of the rhombus is 600 cm², the perimeter (in cm) of the rhombus is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of diagonals = 2 × **Area** = 2 × 600 = 1200.

Identify two numbers with **product 1200** and **difference 10**: 40 and 30.

Semi-diagonals are 20 cm and 15 cm. Using **Pythagorean triplet** (15, 20, 25), the side is 25 cm.

**Perimeter** = 4 × 25 = 100 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Area of **Rhombus** = 600 cm², difference between **diagonals** = 10 cm.

**Formula Used:** Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂; Side (s) = √[(d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²]; Perimeter = 4s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b88b327a0f6a3dd7828dd1d212c16051f7f78a598fb47bc01bdc21f709ced61.png] 

Let the smaller diagonal be **d** cm. Then the longer diagonal is **(d + 10)** cm.

⇒ Area = (1/2) × d × (d + 10) = 600

⇒ d² + 10d = 1200

⇒ d² + 10d − 1200 = 0

⇒ d² + 40d − 30d − 1200 = 0

⇒ d(d + 40) − 30(d + 40) = 0

⇒ (d − 30)(d + 40) = 0

⇒ d = 30 cm (Since length cannot be negative)

⇒ d₁ = 30 cm and d₂ = 30 + 10 = 40 cm

⇒ Side of rhombus (s) = √[(30/2)² + (40/2)²]

⇒ s = √[15² + 20²] = √[225 + 400]

⇒ s = √625 = 25 cm

⇒ **Perimeter** = 4 × 25 = 100 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 100 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All sides are equal, and diagonals bisect each other at 90°. **Opposite angles** are equal, and adjacent angles are supplementary (sum = 180°).

Relation Between Side and Diagonals

The sum of the squares of the diagonals is equal to four times the square of the side: **d₁² + d₂² = 4s²**.

Area of Rhombus

Area can also be calculated using base and height: **Area = Base × Height**, or using trigonometry: **Area = s² × sin(θ)**.

questions.question: Simplify: frac{3+sqrt{6}}{5sqrt{3}-2sqrt{12}-sqrt{32}+sqrt{50}}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Break down the **denominator** terms: 2√12 = 4√3, √32 = 4√2, and √50 = 5√2.

Combine like terms: (5√3 − 4√3) + (5√2 − 4√2) = √3 + √2.

Factorize the **numerator**: 3 + √6 = √3 × √3 + √3 × √2 = √3(√3 + √2).

The expression simplifies to: √3(√3 + √2) ÷ (√3 + √2) = √3.

**∴ The correct answer is √3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** (3 + √6) ÷ (5√3 − 2√12 − √32 + √50)

**Step 1: Simplify the Denominator**

⇒ Denominator = 5√3 − 2√(4 × 3) − √(16 × 2) + √(25 × 2)

⇒ Denominator = 5√3 − 2(2√3) − 4√2 + 5√2

⇒ Denominator = 5√3 − 4√3 − 4√2 + 5√2

⇒ Denominator = (5 − 4)√3 + (5 − 4)√2 = √3 + √2

**Step 2: Factorize the Numerator**

questions.question: The present ages of two sisters are in the ratio 5:7. After 4 years, their ages will be in the ratio 6:8. Find the present age of the younger sister.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare the **ratios**: **Present** (5:7) and **After 4 years** (6:8).

The difference between parts is equal: (6 − 5) = 1 unit and (8 − 7) = 1 unit.

This 1 unit difference corresponds to the **time gap** of 4 years.

⇒ 1 unit = 4 years.

⇒ **Younger sister's present age** = 5 units = 5 × 4 = 20 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio **after 4 years** = 6 : 8

**Calculation:**

Let the present ages be 5x and 7x.

⇒ (5x + 4) / (7x + 4) = 6 / 8

⇒ (5x + 4) / (7x + 4) = 3 / 4

⇒ 4 × (5x + 4) = 3 × (7x + 4)

⇒ 20x + 16 = 21x + 12

⇒ 21x − 20x = 16 − 12

⇒ x = 4

⇒ **Present age of younger sister** = 5x = 5 × 4 = 20 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

questions.question: Three friends Arshdeep, Sandeep and Avtar are on a trip by a car. Arshdeep drives during the first 3 hours at an average speed of 52 km/hr. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **weighted average** formula where **Time** acts as the weight.

Average Speed = (S₁t₁ + S₂t₂ + S₃t₃) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + t₃)

Average Speed = (52 × 3 + 65 × 4 + 76 × 3) ÷ 10

Average Speed = (156 + 260 + 228) ÷ 10 = 644 ÷ 10 = 64.4 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 64.4 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Time spent by **Sandeep** = 4 hr, Speed = 65 km/hr

Time spent by **Avtar** = 3 hr, Speed = 76 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

**Distance** = Speed × Time

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/221cdc67c96e1bb56ec004de73098427de738929f1c78364b283c540e3c936c8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by Arshdeep = 52 × 3 = 156 km

⇒ Distance covered by Sandeep = 65 × 4 = 260 km

⇒ Distance covered by Avtar = 76 × 3 = 228 km

⇒ **Total Distance** = 156 + 260 + 228 = 644 km

⇒ **Total Time** = 3 + 4 + 3 = 10 hr

⇒ **Average Speed** = 644 ÷ 10 = 64.4 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 64.4 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distance

When a person travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Equal Time

If a person travels at speeds x and y for equal intervals of time, the average speed is simply the arithmetic mean: (x + y) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

Speed of one object with respect to another. For opposite directions, add speeds (S₁ + S₂); for the same direction, subtract them (S₁ − S₂).

questions.question: The average of 5 numbers is 18.5. If one number is removed, the average of the remaining 4 numbers becomes 16. Find the number that was removed.

In **averages**, when a value is **removed**, the formula is:

Removed Number = Old Average + [Remaining Count × (Old Average − New Average)]

⇒ Removed Number = 18.5 + [4 × (18.5 − 16)]

⇒ Removed Number = 18.5 + [4 × 2.5] = 18.5 + 10 = 28.5

**∴ The correct answer is 28.5.**

questions.question:
A shopkeeper offers the following schemes on toys of the same marked price.

(A) Successive discounts of 43% and 19% on any number of toys bought.

(B) Successive discounts of 41%, 21% and 49% on any number of toys bought.

(C) 35% discount on the first 5 toys and 3% discount on each toy thereon.

(D) 4 toys free of cost on buying 5 toys.

A customer wants to buy 5 toys. Which of the above schemes is the least beneficial to her?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Scheme A:** Net discount = 43 + 19 − (43 × 19)/100 = 53.83%

**Scheme B:** Successive discounts of 41%, 21% and 49% results in > 70% discount.

**Scheme C:** For exactly 5 toys, the discount is fixed at 35%.

**Scheme D:** Discount % = [Free / Total] × 100 = [4 / (5 + 4)] × 100 ≈ 44.44%

Comparing all: 35% (C) is the **minimum discount**, making it the **least beneficial**.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A customer buys 5 toys of the same **Marked Price (MP)**.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Successive Discount** (x%, y%) = [x + y − (xy / 100)]%

2. **Buy X Get Y Free** Discount % = [Y / (X + Y)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/18803afeaa7da1df7469892774befe9b27c61793416f20dda82bbb376e520d7c.png] 

⇒ **Scheme A:** Successive discounts of 43% and 19%

⇒ Net Discount = 43 + 19 − (43 × 19)/100 = 62 − 8.17 = **53.83%**

⇒ **Scheme B:** Successive 41%, 21% and 49%

⇒ First two: 41 + 21 − (41 × 21)/100 = 62 − 8.61 = 53.39%

⇒ With 49%: 53.39 + 49 − (53.39 × 49)/100 = 102.39 − 26.16 = **76.23%**

⇒ **Scheme C:** Customer buys 5 toys. According to the scheme, the discount is **35%** on the first 5 toys. Since the purchase is exactly 5 toys, the effective discount is **35%**.

⇒ **Scheme D:** 4 toys free on buying 5 toys. Total toys = 5 + 4 = 9.

⇒ Discount % = (4 / 9) × 100 ≈ **44.44%**

⇒ The **least beneficial** scheme is the one with the **lowest discount percentage**.

⇒ Minimum value among {53.83%, 76.23%, 35%, 44.44%} is **35%**.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

In this offer, the customer pays for X items and receives X + Y items. The discount percentage is calculated as [Free Items / Total Items] × 100.

Profit and Loss Relationship

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100.

questions.question: A cricketer has scored an average of 55 runs in 9 matches. In the 10th match, he scores 85 runs. What is his new average?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Extra runs over **average** = 85 − 55 = 30

Distributed increase per match = 30 ÷ 10 = 3

New **average** = 55 + 3 = 58

**∴ The correct answer is 58.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Average** of 9 matches = 55, 10th match **score** = 85

Formula: Total = Average × Number of items

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f879c20ba2d524db419d2acc497dcbadc9526a6c32403ac025d1181f1f12945.png] 

⇒ Total runs in **9 matches** = 55 × 9 = 495

⇒ Total runs in **10 matches** = 495 + 85 = 580

⇒ **New average** = 580 ÷ 10 = 58

**∴ The correct answer is 58.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Deviation Concept

The sum of deviations of all observations from the **average** is always zero. This is used to find the effect of adding or removing an item from the **data set**.

Weighted Average Formula

Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the quantity and A is the **average** of each group.

questions.question: The Anti-Defection Law was introduced through which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**52nd Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Anti-Defection Law** was formally introduced in India through the **52nd Constitutional Amendment Act** in **1985**.
 
• This legislation was enacted during the government of Prime Minister **Rajiv Gandhi** to maintain the stability of elected governments by preventing unethical floor-crossing.
 
• The amendment added the **Tenth Schedule** to the **Constitution of India**, which provides for the disqualification of members of **Parliament** and **State Legislatures** on grounds of defection.
 
• Under this law, a legislator is deemed to have defected if they voluntarily give up the membership of their political party or vote against the party whip without obtaining prior permission.
 
• The power to decide on disqualification rests with the **Speaker** or the **Chairman** of the respective House, whose decision was initially final but later made subject to **Judicial Review** by the **Supreme Court** in the **Kihoto Hollohan case**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **61st Amendment Act**

 
 
• Passed in **1988**, this amendment reduced the minimum voting age from **21 years** to **18 years** for the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assembly** elections.
 
• It amended **Article 326** of the Constitution to encourage greater youth participation in the democratic process.
 
 
 
• **73rd Amendment Act**
 
 
• Enacted in **1992**, it granted constitutional status and protection to the **Panchayati Raj Institutions** (PRIs).
 
• It added **Part IX** and the **Eleventh Schedule** to the Constitution, mandating a three-tier structure of local self-government.
 
 
 
• **44th Amendment Act**
 
 
• Passed in **1978** by the **Janata Government**, it aimed to nullify several controversial changes introduced by the **42nd Amendment** during the **Emergency**.
 
• It replaced the term **internal disturbance** with **armed rebellion** for declaring a **National Emergency** and removed the **Right to Property** from the list of Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: A device driver acts as an interface between which two components?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Operating system and Hardware device**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **device driver** is a specialized type of **software program** that functions as a communication bridge or translator between the **Operating System (OS)** and specific **hardware components**. It allows the OS to interact with hardware without needing to know the precise internal details of how the hardware functions.
 
• The primary role of a driver is **Hardware Abstraction**. By providing a uniform interface, it enables high-level **application software** to perform actions like printing or displaying graphics through the OS, which then passes the request to the driver to execute on the physical **hardware device**.
 
• When an OS issues a generic command (e.g., 'write data to disk'), the **device driver** translates this command into **low-level machine language** or signaling protocols that the hardware controller can interpret. This mechanism ensures **interoperability** across different brands and models of hardware.
 
• Most drivers run in **Kernel Mode**, which is a highly privileged layer of the **Operating System**. This allows the driver to have direct access to **System Memory** and **CPU registers**, ensuring high-speed data transfer through **Direct Memory Access (DMA)** or **Interrupt Requests (IRQ)**.
 
• Without these drivers, a computer would be unable to recognize or utilize peripherals such as **Network Interface Cards (NIC)**, **Graphics Processing Units (GPU)**, **Printers**, or **Sound Cards**, as the OS lacks the built-in logic to communicate with thousands of different hardware variations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Software and User Interaction**:

 
 
• This interface is typically known as the **User Interface (UI)** or **Graphical User Interface (GUI)**. It involves shells like **Windows Explorer** or **macOS Finder** that allow users to launch applications and manage files.
 
 
 
• **CPU and Memory Communication**:
 
 
• Communication between the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** and **Random Access Memory (RAM)** is facilitated by the **Memory Controller** and the **System Bus**, which includes the **Address Bus** and **Data Bus**. This is a hardware-level interaction, not managed by software drivers in the same way peripherals are.
 
 
 
• **User and Computer Interface**:
 
 
• The **Operating System** acts as the master interface between the **User** and the **Computer** hardware. It manages **Resource Allocation**, **Task Scheduling**, and **File Management**, providing the environment in which users can perform computing tasks.
 
 
 
• **Driver Types**:
 
 
• **Virtual Device Drivers (VxD)**: Used to manage **Virtual Machines** or software-simulated hardware.
 
• **Generic Drivers**: Standardized drivers provided by the OS (like **USB Mass Storage** drivers) that work with a wide range of devices without requiring specific manufacturer software.

questions.question: In the search box of File Explorer, which search pattern finds all Word documents in the current folder whose names start with “Unit”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unit*.docx**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Windows File Explorer**, **wildcard characters** are specialized symbols used to represent one or more characters when searching for files or folders. The **asterisk (*)** is the most versatile wildcard, representing a string of **zero or more characters** in a filename.
 
• The search pattern **Unit*** specifies that the filename must begin with the literal string **Unit**. The **asterisk** following it allows for any sequence of characters (including numbers, symbols, or nothing at all) to follow the prefix, ensuring that files like **Unit1**, **Unit_Report**, or just **Unit** are captured.
 
• The **.docx** component of the pattern acts as a filter for the **file extension**. It specifically targets **Microsoft Word Open XML Format** documents created in **Word 2007** and later versions. By combining the prefix and the extension, **Unit*.docx** retrieves only Word files starting with the specified text.
 
• The pattern **Unit*.docx** is the standard syntax because it places the **wildcard** directly between the known prefix and the mandatory extension. This ensures **maximum coverage** for all naming conventions starting with **Unit** without requiring specific characters like spaces or underscores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Incorrect Wildcard Patterns:**

 
 
• ***Unit.docx**: This pattern uses the **asterisk** at the beginning, which directs the search engine to find files that **end with Unit** before the **.docx** extension, such as **ProjectUnit.docx**.
 
• **Unit?.txt**: The **question mark (?)** wildcard represents exactly **one character**. This pattern would find files like **Unit1.txt** or **UnitA.txt**, but it fails the requirement because it targets **plain text files (.txt)** rather than Word documents.
 
• **Unit* .docx**: The inclusion of a **space** between the asterisk and the period is a syntax error for general searches. It would only match files that explicitly contain a **space character** at the end of their name (e.g., **Unit Test .docx**), excluding standard files like **Unit1.docx**.
 
 
 
• **Search Efficiency:** Using **Unit*** in the **File Explorer search box** is non-case-sensitive in **Windows**, meaning it will return results for both **unit*.docx** and **UNIT*.docx**, increasing the search's effectiveness in finding **Word documents**.

questions.question: Gangaikondacholapuram was established as a capital city by which Chola ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajendra I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajendra I**, the son of **Rajaraja I**, established the city of **Gangaikondacholapuram** in the **Ariyalur** district of modern-day **Tamil Nadu** around **1025 CE**.
 
• The city was founded to commemorate his victorious military expedition to **North India**, where his forces reached the **Ganges** river and defeated the **Pala** king, **Mahipala I**.
 
• To celebrate this milestone, he assumed the title **Gangaikonda Chola**, which translates to 'The Chola who conquered the Ganges'.
 
• He shifted the capital of the **Chola Empire** from **Thanjavur** (Tanjore) to **Gangaikondacholapuram**, and it remained the seat of power for nearly 250 years.
 
• He commissioned the construction of a magnificent **Shiva** temple, the **Brihadisvara Temple** of Gangaikondacholapuram, which is recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• To mark the victory, he also excavated a massive irrigation tank called **Cholagangam** (the lake of the Cholas), where water brought from the Ganges was ritually poured.

• **Rajadhiraja I**:
 
 
• The son and successor of **Rajendra I**, known for his military exploits against the **Western Chalukyas**.
 
• He died on the battlefield during the **Battle of Koppam**.
 
 
 
• **Kulottunga I**:

questions.question: The laws to provide for the representation of the Chairpersons of the Panchayats are made by ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Legislature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 243C** of the Indian Constitution, the **State Legislature** is empowered to make laws regarding the **composition of Panchayats**.
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, explicitly states that the **Legislature of a State** may, by law, provide for the representation of the **Chairpersons** of the Panchayats at the **village level** in the Panchayats at the **intermediate level** or the **district level**.
 
• This legislative power also extends to providing representation for the **Chairpersons** of the Panchayats at the **intermediate level** in the Panchayats at the **district level**.
 
• The provision ensures a **vertical linkage** between the three tiers of the **Panchayati Raj Institution (PRI)**, allowing leaders from lower tiers to participate in the planning and execution processes of higher tiers.
 
• The **State Legislature** also determines the manner in which the **Chairperson** of a Panchayat at the village, intermediate, or district level shall be elected, as per **Article 243C(5)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Parliament of India**:

 
 
• While the **Parliament** passed the **73rd Amendment Act** to provide a constitutional framework for **Local Self-Government**, it does not legislate on the specific representation of **Chairpersons** within individual states.
 
• The **Parliament** reserves the power to extend the provisions of **Part IX** to **Scheduled Areas** and **Tribal Areas** under the **PESA Act, 1996**.
 
 
 
• **Governor of State**:
 
 
• The **Governor** has the authority to specify which areas constitute a **village** for the purposes of **Part IX** via public notification under **Article 243(g)**.
 
• However, the **Governor** does not possess the legislative power to frame laws concerning the **representation** of Panchayat members; this remains a **State Legislature** function.
 
 
 
• **The President of India**:
 
 
• The **President** may direct that the provisions of **Part IX** shall apply to any **Union Territory** with such exceptions or modifications as specified under **Article 243L**.
 
• The **President** does not intervene in the legislative domain of states regarding **Panchayat chairpersons' representation**.

questions.question: In which year did the Indian Parliament enact the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act to institutionalise financial discipline and ensure long-term macroeconomic stability?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act** was enacted by the **Indian Parliament** in **2003** to institutionalize **financial discipline** and improve **fiscal management**.
 
• The primary objective of the legislation was to reduce India's **fiscal deficit** and **revenue deficit**, thereby ensuring **long-term macroeconomic stability**.
 
• It mandated the **Central Government** to take necessary steps to limit the **fiscal deficit** to a target of **3% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** over a specified timeframe.
 
• The act aimed to provide a legal framework for **inter-generational equity** in fiscal management and minimize the **public debt** burden on future generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Implementation and Documents:
 
 
• Although enacted in **2003**, the **FRBM Act** officially came into force on **July 5, 2004**.
 
• The act requires the government to present four fiscal policy statements along with the **Union Budget**: the **Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement**, the **Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement**, the **Macroeconomic Framework Statement**, and the **Medium-Term Expenditure Framework**.
 
 
 
• The NK Singh Committee:
 
 
• In **May 2016**, the **Government of India** constituted a committee chaired by **N.K. Singh** to review the working of the **FRBM Act**.
 
• The committee recommended a **Debt-to-GDP ratio** of **60%** for the general government (40% for the Centre and 20% for States) by the year **2023**.
 
 
 
• Escape Clause:
 
 
• The act includes an **Escape Clause** under Section 4(2), which allows the government to relax the **fiscal deficit** target during exceptional times such as **national security**, **war**, **national calamity**, or **structural reforms** in the economy.

questions.question: The incidence of oral cancer in India is strongly linked to the frequent consumption of which of the following harmful substances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tobacco**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The high incidence of **oral cancer** in India is primarily driven by the frequent use of **Tobacco**, which contains over **70 known carcinogens**, including **Tobacco-specific nitrosamines (TSNAs)** like NNN and NNK.
 
• According to clinical data, **oral cavity cancer** accounts for approximately **30 percent** of all cancer types in the country, making it the most common cancer among Indian men.
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** and the **International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC)** have categorized tobacco as a **Group 1 Carcinogen**, indicating a direct causal link to malignancies in the **buccal mucosa**, tongue, and palate.
 
• Frequent consumption of tobacco leads to **Oral Submucous Fibrosis (OSMF)**, a chronic, debilitating, and **premalignant condition** characterized by inflammation and progressive fibrosis of the oral tissues, often resulting in **Squamous Cell Carcinoma**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Forms of Tobacco Use in India:**

 
 
• **Smokeless Tobacco (SLT):** Products like **Khaini**, **Gutkha**, **Zarda**, and **Mawa** are chewed or kept in the mouth, leading to prolonged exposure of the oral lining to harmful chemicals.
 
• **Smoking:** The use of **Bidis** and **Cigarettes** releases **polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons** and carbon monoxide, which further increase the risk of cancers of the floor of the mouth and pharynx.
 
• **Betel Quid (Paan):** Often mixed with tobacco, the **Areca nut** in paan acts as an independent carcinogen, and the addition of **Slaked Lime** enhances the absorption of nicotine and toxins.
 
 
 
• **Analysis of Other Options:**
 
 
• **High-salt diet:** Primarily linked to **hypertension** and **gastric (stomach) cancer**, but it does not have a direct localized carcinogenic effect on the oral cavity.
 
• **Soft drinks and Fried food:** While these contribute to **obesity** and **Type 2 diabetes**, which are general risk factors for metabolic health, they are not primary triggers for oral oncogenesis.

questions.question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution deals specifically with the Union executive structure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part V**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part V** of the **Constitution of India** is titled **The Union** and encompasses **Articles 52 to 151**.
 
• The structure of the **Union Executive** is specifically detailed within **Chapter I** of this Part, covering **Articles 52 to 78**.
 
• The **Union Executive** consists of the **President**, the **Vice-President**, the **Prime Minister**, the **Council of Ministers**, and the **Attorney General of India**.
 
• This Part defines the powers, functions, and election procedures for these offices, establishing the **President** as the constitutional head and the **Prime Minister** as the real executive head under a **parliamentary system**.
 
• Beyond the executive, **Part V** also includes provisions for the **Parliament**, the **Legislative Powers of the President**, the **Union Judiciary (Supreme Court)**, and the **Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part III**:

 
 
• Focuses on **Fundamental Rights** ranging from **Articles 12 to 35**.
 
• It is often referred to as the **Magna Carta** of the Indian Constitution, protecting individual liberties such as **Right to Equality** and **Right to Freedom**.
 
 
 
• **Part IV**:
 
 
• Contains the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** from **Articles 36 to 51**.
 
• These are non-justiciable guidelines for the State to ensure **social and economic justice**.
 
 
 
• **Part VI**:
 
 
• Deals with **The States** and spans from **Articles 152 to 237**.
 
• It defines the structure of the **State Executive** (Governor, Chief Minister), **State Legislature**, and the **High Courts**.

questions.question: Which of the following is included among the water-soluble vitamins collectively grouped together in a specific vitamin class known as vitamin B complex?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thiamin**__.

__
 
• **Thiamin**, chemically identified as **Vitamin B₁**, is a fundamental member of the **Vitamin B complex**, which is a group of **water-soluble vitamins** essential for cellular function.
 
• Its primary biological role is acting as a **coenzyme** (thiamin pyrophosphate) in the **citric acid cycle** and the metabolism of **carbohydrates**, enabling the body to convert nutrients into **adenosine triphosphate (ATP)**.
 
• Because it is **water-soluble**, it is not stored in large amounts in the body and must be consumed regularly through the diet; excess amounts are typically excreted through **urine**.
 
• Severe deficiency of this vitamin leads to **Beriberi**, characterized by **peripheral neuropathy** and **heart failure**, or **Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome**, which primarily affects the **central nervous system**.
 
• Major dietary sources include **fortified grains**, **yeast**, **legumes**, **nuts**, and **pork**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vitamins are broadly classified into two categories: **Fat-soluble** (stored in fatty tissues and the liver) and **Water-soluble** (carried to the body's tissues but not stored).
 
• **Retinol**:
 
 
• Commonly known as **Vitamin A**, it is a **fat-soluble** vitamin essential for **phototransduction** in the retina.

questions.question: In the context of Indian classical music, the term "Khayal" literally signifies which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Imagination or reflective thought**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **Khayal** (also spelled Khyal) is an **Arabic-Persian** loanword that literally translates to **imagination**, **conception**, **fancy**, or **reflective thought**.
 
• In the context of **Indian classical music**, specifically the **Hindustani** tradition, it refers to a modern vocal genre that allows for extensive **improvisation** and **creative freedom** for the performer.
 
• Unlike the older, more structured **Dhrupad** style which focuses on precise syllable articulation and rigid rules, **Khayal** emphasizes the singer's **imaginative treatment** of the **Raga** (melodic framework) through complex ornamentations.
 
• This musical form is characterized by its focus on the **aesthetic beauty** of the notes and the personal **interpretative thought** of the artist, rather than just the rhythmic or lyrical constraints.
 
• The emergence of **Khayal** represented a shift towards more **lyrical** and **ornate** musical expressions, making it the most popular and standard genre of **classical singing** in North India today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Development**:

 
 
• While its roots are sometimes traced back to the **13th century** and **Amir Khusrau**, the modern **Khayal** format was popularized in the **18th century** Mughal court of **Muhammad Shah 'Rangila'**.
 
• The legendary musicians **Nyamat Khan** (known by the pen name **Sadarang**) and his nephew **Firoz Khan** (**Adarang**) are credited with composing numerous **Bandishes** (compositions) that elevated **Khayal** to its supreme status.
 
 
 
• **Structural Components**:
 
 
• A typical performance includes **Bada Khayal** (great Khayal), sung in a slow tempo or **Vilambit Laya**, and **Chhota Khayal** (small Khayal), sung in a fast tempo or **Drut Laya**.
 
• The lyrics, known as the **Bandish**, usually consist of two parts: the **Sthayi** (initial phrase) and the **Antara** (second half).
 
• Commonly used **Talas** (rhythmic cycles) for this style include **Ektal**, **Teental**, **Tilwada**, and **Jhumra**.
 
 
 
• **Gharanas**:
 
 
• The tradition of **Khayal** is preserved through various **Gharanas** (lineages/schools) such as **Gwalior** (the oldest), **Agra**, **Kirana**, **Jaipur-Atrauli**, and **Patiala**, each having a unique approach to **reflective improvisation**.

questions.concept: External Sector and Currency Exchange rate
questions.question: In the Balance of Payments, an increase in foreign exchange reserves appears under which category?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Capital Account - Debit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Balance of Payments (BoP)** is a comprehensive statistical statement that summarizes the economic transactions of a country with the rest of the world during a specific period. It follows a **double-entry bookkeeping** system where every transaction is recorded as either a **Credit** or a **Debit**.
 
• In BoP terminology, any transaction that leads to an **inflow of foreign exchange** into the country is recorded as a **Credit (+)**, while any transaction resulting in an **outflow of foreign exchange** is recorded as a **Debit (−)**.
 
• **Foreign Exchange Reserves** (including foreign currencies, **Gold**, and **Special Drawing Rights**) are managed by the **Central Bank** (such as the **Reserve Bank of India**). When there is a surplus in the overall BoP, the Central Bank buys foreign currency to prevent the domestic currency from appreciating excessively, thereby **increasing the reserves**.
 
• Since the purchase of foreign assets/currencies involves an **outflow of domestic funds** to acquire those assets, an **increase in official reserves** is recorded as a **Debit** entry in the **Capital Account** (or the **Official Reserve Account**, which is a sub-component of the Capital/Financial account).
 
• Conversely, if the country faces a **BoP deficit**, the Central Bank sells its reserves to meet the shortage of foreign exchange. This **decrease in reserves** represents an inflow of foreign exchange into the system and is recorded as a **Credit** entry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Current Account**:

 
 
• It records the export and import of **visible goods** (merchandise trade) and **invisible services** (like shipping, banking, and insurance).
 
• It also includes **unilateral transfers** (gifts, remittances, and donations) and **income receipts/payments** (interest, profits, and dividends).
 
• A **Current Account Debit** occurs when a country imports more than it exports or makes transfer payments abroad.
 
 
 
• **Capital Account**:
 
 
• It records transactions that cause a change in the **assets or liabilities** of the residents of a country or its government.
 
• Key components include **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, **Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI)**, **External Commercial Borrowings (ECB)**, and **Banking Capital**.
 
• A **Capital Account Credit** occurs during **borrowings** from abroad or **disinvestment** (sale of assets), as these bring foreign exchange into the country.

questions.question: Why do noble gases exist as gases at room temperature, while halogens exist as solids, liquids, or gases down the group?

options.text: Larger atomic size of noble gases
Weak intermolecular forces in noble gases
Strong chemical bonds in noble gases

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weak intermolecular forces in noble gases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Noble gases**, belonging to **Group 18** of the periodic table, have a completely filled valence shell electronic configuration (**ns²np⁶**), except for Helium (**1s²**).
 
• Due to this stable octet, noble gas atoms do not readily share or transfer electrons to form **covalent** or **ionic bonds** under standard conditions, causing them to exist as **monatomic** atoms.
 
• The only attractive forces existing between these monatomic atoms are extremely weak **London Dispersion Forces** (a type of **Van der Waals force**), which arise from temporary dipoles.
 
• Because these **intermolecular forces** are so weak, the thermal energy available at **room temperature** (approximately 298 K) is more than sufficient to overcome the attraction, keeping the atoms in a **gaseous state**.
 
• As a result, noble gases have very low **melting** and **boiling points** compared to other elements in the same period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Halogens (Group 17)**:

 
 
• Unlike noble gases, halogens exist as **diatomic molecules** (F₂, Cl₂, Br₂, I₂).
 
• Down the group, the **atomic size** and the number of electrons increase, which enhances the **polarizability** of the molecule.
 
• Stronger polarizability leads to stronger **London Dispersion Forces**. This is why **Fluorine** and **Chlorine** are gases, **Bromine** is a liquid, and **Iodine** is a solid at room temperature.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity and Bonding**:
 
 
• **High reactivity**: Noble gases are actually known for their **chemical inertness** or low reactivity due to high **ionization enthalpy** and stable configurations.
 
• **Strong chemical bonds**: Noble gases do not form strong bonds in their elemental form; strong **interatomic** forces only appear in compounds like **Xenon tetrafluoride** (XeF₄), which are formed under specific conditions.

questions.question: In a sound wave traveling through air, which of the following terms refers to a region where the particles are crowded together, resulting in high pressure and high density?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Compression**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sound waves are categorized as **longitudinal mechanical waves**, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth in the same direction as the wave propagation.
 
• A **Compression** is a region in a longitudinal wave where the particles of the medium are **temporarily crowded** together due to the external force of a vibrating object.
 
• Because the particles are packed into a smaller volume, this region is characterized by **high density** and **high pressure** relative to the average state of the medium.
 
• Scientifically, the **pressure** of a medium is directly proportional to its **density**; thus, when particles are forced together in a compression, both values peak simultaneously.
 
• On a graphical representation (pressure-distance graph), a compression is depicted as the **crest** or the highest point of the curve, representing maximum disturbance from the equilibrium position.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rarefaction**:

 
 
• This is the region of a longitudinal wave where the particles are **spread apart**.
 
• It is associated with **low density** and **low pressure**, appearing as a **trough** on a pressure-distance graph.
 
 
 
• **Wavelength**:
 
 
• It is defined as the **physical distance** between two consecutive compressions or two consecutive rarefactions.
 
• In the International System of Units (SI), wavelength is measured in **meters (m)**.
 
 
 
• **Crest**:
 
 
• This term is primarily used for **transverse waves** (like light or ripples on water) to describe the point of maximum upward displacement.
 
• In sound wave analysis, while the term **compression** describes the physical state, 'crest' is often the mathematical label for that peak in a sine wave model.

questions.question: Which type of Centre-State relation is covered under Articles 245 to 255 of Part XI of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Legislative relations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part XI** of the **Indian Constitution** is divided into two chapters, where **Chapter I**, comprising **Articles 245 to 255**, specifically governs the **Legislative relations** between the Union and the States.
 
• **Article 245** defines the territorial extent of laws, stating that **Parliament** can make laws for the whole or any part of **India**, while a **State Legislature** can make laws for the whole or any part of that specific state.
 
• **Article 246** deals with the subject matter of laws, utilizing the **Seventh Schedule** which contains the **Union List**, **State List**, and **Concurrent List** to distribute power.
 
• **Article 248** grants **Residuary powers** of legislation exclusively to the **Parliament**, covering any matter not enumerated in the Concurrent or State Lists.
 
• **Article 249** and **Article 250** empower the **Parliament** to legislate on matters in the **State List** under specific circumstances, such as in the **national interest** (upon a Rajya Sabha resolution) or during a **Proclamation of Emergency**.
 
• **Article 254** handles the doctrine of **Repugnancy**, ensuring that if a state law conflicts with a central law on a **Concurrent List** subject, the central law prevails to maintain constitutional consistency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administrative relations**:

 
 
• These are detailed in **Chapter II** of **Part XI**, spanning **Articles 256 to 263**, focusing on the executive powers and coordination between the Centre and States.
 
 
 
• **Financial relations**:
 
 
• These relations are primarily contained in **Part XII** of the Constitution, from **Articles 264 to 293**, covering the distribution of **taxes**, **grants-in-aid**, and the **Finance Commission** (Article 280).
 
 
 
• **Judicial system**:
 
 
• India possesses an **integrated judicial system**; therefore, unlike legislative or executive powers, there is no strict federal division of judicial relations. The **Supreme Court** and **High Courts** form a single hierarchy.

questions.question:
An image‑editing program and a video‑editing program both use the same shared library for color correction.

Which advantage of modular application software does this situation show?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Code reusability across different applications**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Modular application software** is a design technique that emphasizes separating the functionality of a program into independent, interchangeable **modules**.
 
• A **shared library** is a file that contains code and data that can be used by multiple programs at the same time, promoting the concept of **Write Once, Run Anywhere** within a system.
 
• In this scenario, the **color correction** logic is encapsulated within a single library. Since both the **image-editing** and **video-editing** programs utilize this same resource, the developer avoids duplicating the complex algorithms for color grading in two separate places.
 
• This practice is the definition of **code reusability**, which significantly reduces **development time**, minimizes the **memory footprint** of the software, and ensures that improvements made to the library benefit all connected applications simultaneously.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Modular Design Benefits**:

 
 
• **Easier Maintenance**: Bug fixes or updates performed on the **shared library** automatically propagate to both programs without needing to recompile the individual applications.
 
• **Interoperability**: It allows different software systems to work together and share common **data processing** protocols.
 
• **Efficiency**: It reduces **redundancy** because the system does not need to store multiple copies of the same logic on the **hard drive** or in **RAM**.
 
 
 
• **Analysis of Other Concepts**:
 
 
• **Redundancy**: In computing, **redundancy** refers to the duplication of components or functions. Modular software using shared libraries actually **decreases redundancy** by centralizing functions.
 
• **Dependencies**: Modular software actually creates **dependencies** (the program depends on the library to run). Shared libraries do not remove dependencies; they manage them through **dynamic linking**.
 
• **Offline Operation**: Whether a program is **modular** or uses **shared libraries** has no direct correlation with its ability to function without an internet connection.

questions.question: Which of the following features at Lothal provides the most convincing evidence of its role as a maritime trading centre in the Harappan Civilization?

options.text: Discovery of seals indicating contacts with distant regions
A brick-built basin connected to an ancient river channel
Evidence of bead-making workshops within the settlement
A large warehouse located near the dock structure

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A brick-built basin connected to an ancient river channel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lothal**, located in the modern-day state of **Gujarat**, served as a vital industrial and commercial hub of the **Indus Valley Civilization** (Harappan Civilization) around **2400 BCE**.
 
• The most distinctive feature of **Lothal** is its **brick-built basin**, which is widely identified by archaeologists as the world's earliest known **artificial dockyard**.
 
• This structure was designed with advanced hydraulic engineering, featuring a rectangular basin measuring approximately **218 meters** in length and **37 meters** in width, constructed entirely of **baked bricks**.
 
• It was strategically connected via an **inlet channel** to an ancient course of the **Bhogavo River**, a tributary of the **Sabarmati**, allowing ships to enter the basin during **high tide**.
 
• The presence of a **sluice gate** mechanism helped maintain the water level within the basin, facilitating the **berthing and loading** of seafaring vessels, which provides the most direct and convincing evidence of its role as a **maritime trading centre**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trade and Infrastructure**:

 
 
• The **Warehouse**: A massive wooden structure (now only the mud-brick platforms remain) situated next to the dockyard was used to store cargo, indicating organized **international trade**.
 
• **Seals**: The discovery of **Persian Gulf seals** (circular button seals) at the site confirms direct maritime links with **Mesopotamia** and the **Dilmun** civilization (modern Bahrain).
 
• **Bead-making Industry**: **Lothal** was a major production center for **carnelian** and **steatite beads**, which were highly valued export items found across Western Asia.
 
• **Excavation**: The site was discovered and excavated by the renowned archaeologist **S.R. Rao** in **1954**.
